newsitem.title: USA: Sierra Power return sharing biggest giveback.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Power return sharing biggest giveback.

text.p: Sierra Pacific Power Co's agreement to split return on equity of more than 12 percent with its electric and gas customers was the utility's biggest giveback in a recent rate proposal, a company spokeswoman said Wednesday.

Sierra Pacific, based in Reno, Nev., also agreed with the staff of the Public Service Commission of Nevada and the Office of Consumer Advocate to give Nevada electricity customers a $13 million refund, cut rates by $7.1 million, and then freeze rates until January, 2000.
The proposal is similar to a rate filing submitted in September, but the earlier proposal alloted some refund and rate reduction to gas customers as well as power ratepayers.
The agreement also allows Sierra Pacific to use any return on equity above 12 percent to buy down long-term fuel or power purchase contracts.
"We would probably do that before we would give another refund to customers in order to be in a more competitive position after the three-year rate freeze," said spokeswoman Pat Englin.
The Nevada commission is expected to decide February 6 on the rate plan, which would be retroactive to January 1.
Sierra Pacific serves 250,000 customers in Nevada and California.
